title: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)

sections.label: Fraud and market misconduct examples
sections.summary: Examples include a billion-dollar nickel trading scheme, oil trade financing fraud with about US$3.5 billion bank exposure, and stock market misconduct cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Several examples, some of which I have gleaned from the CAD's Annual Report 2020/21, include the fraudulent billion-dollar investment scheme by nickel trading companies; trade financing fraud involving several oil trading companies that has left banks with a combined exposure reported to be about US$3.5 billion; and numerous cases of misconduct in the stock markets.

sections.label: Whistle-blowing legislation suggestion
sections.summary: A suggestion is made for whistle-blowing legislation that protects whistle-blowers and incentivises them when information leads to prosecution and asset recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: One suggestion I wish to make is to have a whistle-blowing legislation that not only protects whistle-blowers from recrimination but also incentivises them should the information they provide lead to successful prosecution and recovery of ill-gotten assets.

sections.label: CAD Wirecard investigation
sections.summary: The CAD investigated Wirecard, involving alleged losses over €1 billion and ongoing Singapore prosecution; the report found the auditor lacked sufficient professional scepticism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: By the way, the CAD has investigated Wirecard, too, which involves alleged losses of more than €1 billion and prosecution in Singapore is currently afoot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The report concluded that the auditor did not maintain sufficient professional scepticism and this led to it accepting documents and instructions without sufficient scrutiny.

sections.label: Paying CAOs market value
sections.summary: The passage states CAO officers remain highly sought after in the private sector and should be paid as close as possible to market value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: After all, its officers continue to be highly sought after in the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We must acknowledge this and pay our CAOs as close as possible to their market value.

sections.label: Death penalty considerations
sections.summary: The Government considers seriousness of the offence, how widespread it is, and need for deterrence; mandatory death penalty applies to listed main offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Government's position was spelt out by the hon Minister on 5 October 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He said that in determining whether to apply the death penalty to a particular offence, the Government takes into account three considerations in totality: seriousness of the offence; how widespread the offence is; and the need for deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Applying these considerations, the main offences for which the mandatory death penalty is imposed are intentional murder, gang robbery with murder, trafficking of significant quantities of drugs, terrorist bombing and use of firearms.

sections.label: Life sentences for drug couriers
sections.summary: Drug couriers convicted of capital drug trafficking offences with certificates of substantial assistance or abnormality of mind receive life sentences instead of the mandatory death penalty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Drug couriers convicted of capital drug trafficking offences who have been issued with certificates of substantial assistance to curtail drug trafficking activities or found to be suffering from abnormality of mind would be imposed with life sentences instead of the mandatory death penalty.

sections.label: Couriers given substantial assistance certificates
sections.summary: Between 1 January 2013 and 11 February 2022, 82 of 104 convicted drug couriers received certificates of substantial assistance and life imprisonment terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Minister had revealed earlier last month that for the period between 1 January 2013 and 11 February 2022, out of 104 accused persons who were found to be couriers and convicted as drug traffickers, 82 of them received certificates of substantial assistance and they were imposed with life imprisonment terms.

sections.label: Couriers given mandatory death penalties
sections.summary: 13% of couriers convicted of capital drug trafficking charges were imposed with mandatory death penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In other words, 13% were found to be couriers and convicted of capital drug trafficking charges were imposed with mandatory death penalties.

sections.label: Death penalty offences in Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore uses the death penalty for a very small number of offences, with drug trafficking receiving the largest number of death sentences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the death penalty is used only for a very small number of offences, including for murder, kidnapping, illegal use of firearms and drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Of these, the largest number of death sentences are meted out for drug trafficking.

sections.label: Singapore drug addiction and crime rates
sections.summary: Singapore's rate of drug addiction and drug-related crimes is amongst the lowest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While drug-related offences are more widespread, in relative terms, compared to other countries, Singapore’s rate of drug addiction and drug-related crimes is amongst the lowest in the world.

sections.label: Commissioner reviews findings and varies punishments
sections.summary: The Commissioner reviews findings and can vary punishments, with the process starting and ending within the Singapore Prison Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Commissioner also reviews the findings and has the authority to vary punishments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the process starts and ends within the Singapore Prison Service, which investigates, presses charges and recommends punishment.

sections.label: Inmates thanking staff after caning
sections.summary: According to one published account, inmates are sometimes required to thank prison staff after being caned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On caning, lastly, according to one published account, there is a practice that sometimes happens of requiring inmates to "thank" the prison staff after being caned.

sections.label: Community programmes and recidivism rate
sections.summary: Community-based programme participation rose over 40%, with 90% completing, contributing to a two-year recidivism rate of 20% for 2018 releases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Currently, the number of inmates participating in community-based programmes to help their rehabilitation has increased by more than 40%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: An impressive 90% of these inmates successfully complete the programmes too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I believe that all these efforts have been instrumental in SPS achieving a commendable all-time two-year low recividism rate of 20% for inmates released in 2018.

sections.label: Drug offenders and drug abuse rates
sections.summary: About 70% of penal inmates are drug offenders, and Singapore has about 30 opiate abusers per 100,000 versus 600 in the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Almost 70% of our penal inmate population consists of drug offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: We have an uncompromising stance on drugs that allowed us to have one of the lowest rates of drug abuse in the world – about 30 opiate abusers per 100,000, compared to 600 per 100,000 in the US.

sections.label: Two-year and five-year recidivism
sections.summary: The two-year recidivism rate for the 2019 release cohort is 20%, while the five-year rate is double that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The two-year rate for the 2019 release cohort is 20%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, as has been pointed out in this House before, the five-year recidivism rate is double that.

sections.label: Programmes tapering off after two years
sections.summary: Programmes including the Mandatory Aftercare Scheme taper off around the two-year point, which the speaker deduces may explain rising recidivism after two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Most of these appear to taper off at around the two-year point, including the Mandatory Aftercare Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will, therefore, venture to deduce that the reason or at least one of the reasons, why the recidivism rate goes up after the two-year mark is precisely because Government programmes are tapering off.

sections.label: Residents' views on death penalty
sections.summary: A 2019 MHA-commissioned study found most Singapore residents felt the death penalty was more effective than life imprisonment for serious crimes including drug trafficking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A study commissioned by MHA in 2019 on the views of Singapore residents found that the majority felt that the death penalty was more effective than life imprisonment for serious crimes, including drug trafficking.

sections.label: Prison learning and upskilling initiatives
sections.summary: Prisons and Yellow Ribbon Singapore facilitate inmate learning, including the Train and Place and Grow initiative offering certificates and diplomas such as media skills training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Prisons and Yellow Ribbon Singapore have done a good job in facilitating inmates' learning and upskilling even while they are in prison.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am especially encouraged to know about the Train and Place (TAP) and Grow initiative, where the inmates are offered the opportunity to acquire certificates and complete diploma courses in certain fields, such as media skills training, while in prison.

sections.label: Inmate job programme and TAP Grow
sections.summary: The passage asks how successful the programme is in helping inmates secure and retain jobs, and whether TAP and Grow will extend to other industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide more information about how successful the programme has been in helping inmates not just to secure jobs after their release, but in equipping them with the necessary skills to sustain and retain their jobs in the long term?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, are there any plans to extend the TAP and Grow initiative to other industries?

sections.label: Police Cameras case solving
sections.summary: Since their installation in 2012, Police Cameras have aided officers to solve more than 5,000 cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Since their installation in 2012, Police Cameras have aided our officers to solve more than 5,000 cases.

sections.label: Police camera surveillance expansion plans
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Police plan to increase camera and surveillance use and whether technology developments will make cameras less costly and more widespread.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Are there any plans by the Police to increase the use of cameras and surveillance where needed and do the developments in technology mean that the use of these cameras would be less costly in the coming years and therefore, more widespread?

sections.label: Automated immigration clearance for all travellers
sections.summary: The passage asks about automating contactless immigration clearance, notes ICA's announcement that all travellers can use automated lanes next year, and hopes Singaporeans' clearance time does not increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: Is there scope to leverage technology to simplify and automate immigration clearance processes and make them contactless, as far as possible?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I note with interest, the recent announcement by ICA that, from next year, all travellers will be able to use the automated immigration clearance lanes, previously reserved for Singaporeans and PRs, upon arrival in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This should reduce immigration clearance time for foreigners entering Singapore while reducing the manpower strain on ICA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I do hope, however, that such a move, does not result in the unintended consequence of increasing the immigration clearance time for Singaporeans.

sections.label: ICA move and Singaporeans' clearance time
sections.summary: The passage invites the Minister to share whether ICA's move will affect immigration clearance time for Singaporeans and whether dedicated lanes can be reserved for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In the premise, I invite the Minister to share with this House whether the move taken by ICA will affect immigration clearance time for Singaporeans and whether a dedicated lane or two can still be reserved for the exclusive use of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Incarceration and pace of change
sections.summary: The passage states the men are serving time for offences, and that technology and a quickening pace of life make a year behind bars different from a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: These men are serving time for the offences committed, a necessary tenet of the law and order that keeps our nation safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, with the quickening pace of life and changes brought about by technology, a year behind bars today is different from the same 12 months one decade a week ago.

sections.label: Youth under 30 new abusers
sections.summary: CNB reported that youth aged under 30 continued to form around 60% of new abusers in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: CNB reported that youth aged under 30 continued to form around 60% of new abusers in recent years.

sections.label: New psychoactive substances and digital dealing
sections.summary: New psychoactive substances are rising and hard to detect or regulate, and traffickers and youth abusers use e-commerce and encrypted messaging apps like Telegram to transact swiftly and anonymously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, drugs in the form of new psychoactive substances are on the rise and these are not easy to detect or as straightforward to regulate or enforce from a legislative standpoint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, drug traffickers and youth abusers utilise e-commerce services and encrypted messaging apps like Telegram, enabling them to transact swiftly and anonymously in the digital space.

sections.label: First-time and repeat young abusers
sections.summary: 75% of young drug abuse arrests were first-time abusers and repeat young abusers doubled over the last couple of years, with a liberal attitude among young people towards drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: With 75% of young drug abuse arrests being first-time drug abusers and the number of repeat young drug abusers doubling over the last couple of years, there is a distressingly liberal attitude among young people today towards drugs and other such substances.

sections.label: Malay drug offender statistics decline
sections.summary: Malay drug offenders arrested last year declined 15% versus 7% for other communities, new Malay offenders declined 32% and were fewer than the Chinese community, credited to CNB, MHA and the Dadah Itu Haram campaign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Recent statistics show that the number of Malay drug offenders arrested last year declined by 15%, compared to offenders from other communities which declined by only 7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The number of new Malay drug offenders declined by 32% and the number of new Malay offenders was less than the Chinese community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For me, this is something very encouraging to our community and it is the result of efforts by CNB and MHA over the years, especially the “Dadah Itu Haram” campaign which began in April 2017 in support of our Malay/Muslim community’s initiatives.

sections.label: Prisoner's medical conditions and appointments
sections.summary: Eleven medical conditions, 13 prescription medications and eight appointments he would have had to cross the island to attend.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Eleven medical conditions, 13 medications on prescription, eight appointments which he would have had to cross the island to attend.

sections.label: Handover medical care for released prisoners
sections.summary: The question asks what is being done to improve handover medical care when prisoners with multiple medical conditions are released to the community, especially if existing follow-up is far from home.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Can the Minister tell us what is being done to improve handover medical care when prisoners with multiple medical conditions are released and returned to the community, especially if their are existing follow-up is far from home?

sections.label: NS officers in Home Team
sections.summary: More than a quarter of a million NS officers have served or are serving in the Home Team, and this year marks NS55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: They stand shoulder-to-shoulder with our regulars, keeping Singapore safe and secure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We now have more than a quarter of a million NS officers who have served or are serving in the Home Team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This year also marks the 55th anniversary of National Service in Singapore, or NS55, for short.

sections.label: Home Team NSmen support disparity
sections.summary: An NSman who served in both SAF and Home Team senses Home Team NSmen are not treated on par or given same support as SAF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Having the benefit of serving both in the SAF and the Home Team as an NSman, I get a sense that Home Team NSmen are not treated on par and given the same level of support as those serving in the SAF, possibly because of the lack of resources.

sections.label: Review of online harms levers
sections.summary: Government signaled intention to review feasibility of regulatory levers for online harms; Ministry asked for update on legislation and timeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Last year, the Government had signaled its intention to review the feasibility of regulatory levers to enable the Government to deal with online harms effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the review, in particular, what legislation with regard to levers, platforms and content, and what is the timeline?

sections.label: Scams, money mules, security benchmarks
sections.summary: Police investigated 157 people for scams or money mule operations, and over 7,000 scammers and money mules were arrested in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last month, the Police investigated 157 people for suspected involvement in scams or money mule operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 2021, the Singapore Police Force arrested and investigated more than 7,000 scammers and money mules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How can we prevent people from becoming money mules?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And they seem to become younger than before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In addition to public education and campaigns, would the Ministry consider new measures in collaboration with e-financial institutions?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: From the NSRS and then WSQ skills requirements and licensing of individual officers, annual assessment of security agencies, implementation of the Progressive Wage Model in 2016 and the launch of the security industry transformation map in 2018, officers and agencies have regularly been subjected to tighter and higher benchmarks.

sections.label: Cheap-sourcing in security industry
sections.summary: Union of Security Employees says many buyers use cheap-sourcing, asking three quotes by headcount and choosing cheapest rates, especially in private residential sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Sad to say, the Union of Security Employees has shared with me that many buyers today still engage in "cheap-sourcing" instead. "Cheap-sourcing" is easy to implement – ask for three quotes by headcount basis and whoever supplies the security officers at the cheapest rates gets the job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Whether the number of security officers or the skillsets of the security officers are adequate for the site is usually not the key deciding factor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: This is especially so for the private residential sector, which is estimated to be about 25% of sites procuring private security in Singapore. "Cheap-sourcing" often leads to poor outcomes and low productivity.

sections.label: Security sector headcounts mentality
sections.summary: The sector needs to progress beyond a headcounts mentality, a big reason it faces an estimated shortfall of 10,000 to 15,000 officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We need to help the sector progress beyond this "headcounts" mentality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I think it is a big reason why the sector continues to face an estimated shortfall of 10,000 to 15,000 officers today.

sections.label: Police officer job conditions
sections.summary: Job conditions for officers can improve if operating models and practices shift decisively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Job conditions for our officers can become much better if operating models and practices shift decisively.

sections.label: Crime and scam losses
sections.summary: SPF reported over 46,000 crimes, the highest in a decade, driven by scam cases four times that in 2017, with victims losing $635 million last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: SPF reported over 46,000 crimes, the highest in the decade, driven by scam cases being four times that in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: Last year, scam victims lost a total of $635 million.

sections.label: Anti-Scam Centre partnerships
sections.summary: SPF's Anti-Scam Centre froze 24,000 bank accounts and recovered over $160 million in scam proceeds, and MHA was asked how it will step up public and private partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: SPF has established the Anti-Scam Centre, which has proven effective in our fight against scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: This partnership with stakeholders across the payments value chain seems to have borne fruit, with 24,000 bank accounts frozen and over $160 million in scam proceeds recovered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: On this note, how will MHA step up partnerships with both public and private stakeholders in the digital ecosystem?

sections.label: MHA 2022 Budget manpower
sections.summary: Noting a modest 1.8% increase in MHA's 2022 Budget, the Minister was asked to clarify if expenditures planned for additional manpower and capabilities to stem scam growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: In noting the modest 1.8% increase in MHA's 2022 Budget, can the Minister clarify if the expenditures have planned for additional manpower as well as capabilities so that our Police can be more effective in stemming the growth of scam cases to keep Singapore safe and secure?

sections.label: Section 377A and LGBTQ+ protection
sections.summary: While section 377A remains on the books, there will be no proactive enforcement, and the MRHA makes attacks on LGBTQ+ persons an offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Government has thus taken the approach that while section 377A remains on the books, there will be no proactive enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We expressly included in the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act (MRHA) that any attack on LGBTQ+ groups or on persons because they are LGBTQ+ will be an offence and will not be tolerated.

sections.label: Government considering way forward
sections.summary: The Government is considering the best way forward, respecting different viewpoints and avoiding a sudden destabilising change in social norms and public expectations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Government is considering the best way forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We must respect the different viewpoints, consider them carefully, talk to the different groups and if and when we decide to move, we will do so in a way that continues to balance between these different viewpoints and avoids causing a sudden destabilising change in social norms and public expectations.

sections.label: Deterrent impact of death penalty
sections.summary: The passage states the death penalty has had a clear, strong deterrent impact based on past behaviour and current trends.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In our view, it has had a clear, strong deterrent impact, based on past behaviour, as well, as current trends.

sections.label: Regional survey on death penalty
sections.summary: 82% of regional respondents believed the death penalty makes people not want to commit serious crimes, and 69% found it more effective than life imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We wanted to get a sense of what people in these places knew and thought.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And this is what we found: 82% of respondents believed that DP makes people not to want to commit serious crimes in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: These are not Singaporeans, these are people in the region – 69% believed that the DP is more effective in discouraging people from committing serious crimes, compared to life imprisonment.

sections.label: Reduction in average net weight trafficked
sections.summary: Comparing four years before and after, there was a 66% reduction in the average net weight trafficked.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Comparing the four years before and after, there was a 66% reduction in the average net weight trafficked.

sections.label: Survey on mandatory death penalty appropriateness
sections.summary: 81% said the mandatory death penalty was appropriate for intentional murder, 71% for firearm offences, 66% for drug trafficking, and over 80% believed it deterred these offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the question as to whether the MDP is appropriate: 81% said it was appropriate for intentional murder; 71% said it was appropriate for firearm offences; 66% said that it was appropriate for drug trafficking; and more than 80% also believed that the DP had deterred the commission of these offences in Singapore.

sections.label: US drug overdose deaths estimate
sections.summary: A CDC report estimates more than 100,000 drug overdose deaths in the US in the year ending April 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A CDC report estimates that more than 100,000 drug overdose deaths in the US took place in the one-year period ending April 2021.

sections.label: Baltimore drug spending and violence
sections.summary: In Baltimore, drug spending is estimated at US$165 million with over 19,000 heroin users, and violence is part of their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In Baltimore, spending on drugs is estimated at an incredible US$165 million, with over 19,000 heroin users.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Criminal records and poor job prospects push them into the drug trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And violence is part and parcel of their lives; either they use violence or it is used on them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And the impact of drugs on innocent children and babies is rarely ever discussed.

sections.label: Newborns diagnosed with NAS daily
sections.summary: Based on 2017 data, nearly 80 newborns are diagnosed with Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome every day.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Based on the 2017 data, nearly 80 newborns are diagnosed with Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome (NAS) every day.

sections.label: CNB arrests over time
sections.summary: In the 1990s, CNB arrested about 6,000 abusers per year, and now arrests about 3,000 to 3,500 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the 1990s, CNB arrested about 6,000 abusers per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Now, it arrests about 3,000 to 3,500 per year.

sections.label: Families and low crime
sections.summary: It is not just them but their families, and crime has been kept low in Singapore because drug abuse has been kept low.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And it is not just them, if you consider their families.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And crime has been kept low in Singapore because the drugs abuse situation has been kept low.

sections.label: Drugs and US homelessness
sections.summary: The drug problem has also contributed to the homelessness situation in many major US cities.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The drug problem has also contributed to the homelessness situation in many major US cities.

sections.label: Singapore drug abusers remain low
sections.summary: The number of drug abusers in Singapore remains low, though there are some worrying trends.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: My answer is that the number of drug abusers in Singapore remains low, though there are some worrying trends.

sections.label: Removing DP and syndicates
sections.summary: If the DP were removed, more drug syndicates and traffickers would bring larger amounts of drugs into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If we removed the DP, I have no doubt, more drug syndicates and traffickers will bring larger amounts of drugs into Singapore.

sections.label: No CSA after defence
sections.summary: The purpose will be undermined if offenders fight a case, offer information later and ask for a CSA, so this move is not intended.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The purpose will be undermined, if we allow offenders to fight a case, put up a defence based on other legal arguments and then offer the information later and ask for a CSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, we do not intend to make that move.

sections.label: Recidivism rates
sections.summary: The two-year recidivism rate is 20% for the most recent release cohort, and the five-year rate for the 2016 cohort is 41%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Our two-year recidivism rate is the lowest it has been. 20% for the most recent release cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The five-year recidivism rate for the 2016 release cohort is higher, at 41%.

sections.label: Yellow Ribbon volunteers
sections.summary: There are over 1,200 grassroots volunteers under the Yellow Ribbon Community Project, involving all 93 divisions across Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Today, there are over 1,200 grassroots volunteers under the Yellow Ribbon Community Project, involving all 93 divisions across Singapore.

sections.label: NITEC Services programme graduates
sections.summary: Prisons and Yellow Ribbon Singapore worked with ITE to introduce the NITEC in Services – Business Services Programme, and the first batch of 29 graduated in February this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Last year, Prisons and Yellow Ribbon Singapore (YRSG) worked with ITE to introduce the NITEC in Services – Business Services Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The first batch of 29 graduated in February this year.

sections.label: Inmate training and jobs
sections.summary: Some released inmates work in media-related jobs; 30 inmates were in the first precision engineering and logistics training batch, and about 650 inmates will benefit yearly from TAP and Grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Some of them have since been released and they are working in media-related jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There were 30 inmates from the first batch of training programmes for precision engineering and logistics and about 650 inmates will benefit from the TAP and Grow initiative in these three sectors every year.

sections.label: Community rehabilitation supervisees
sections.summary: As at end of 2021, about 3,400 supervisees were undergoing rehabilitation in the community, double the number from five years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As at end of 2021, there were about 3,400 supervisees undergoing rehabilitation in the community, double the number from five years ago.

sections.label: Replicating investigative mechanism outside Government
sections.summary: Speaker questions how an entire investigative mechanism outside Government could be replicated and at what cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If that is the suggestion, if I understood him correctly, I would suggest it does not make much sense because how do you replicate, and at what cost an entire investigative mechanism outside the Government?

sections.label: New Zealand, China, McClay donations
sections.summary: A Financial Times article described New Zealand as on the edge of viability, and McClay received NZ$150,000 from a China-based businessman.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A Financial Times article this month said that New Zealand was "on the edge of viability as a member" of its allied relationships because of its "supine attitude towards China" and "compromised political system".

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: McClay is infamous for receiving NZ$150,000 from a China-based businessman, Lang Lin.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: New Zealand allows donations from New Zealand-registered companies even if they are foreign-owned.

sections.label: Complaint channels against Ministers
sections.summary: Civil servants can take complaints about a Minister to higher authority, with AGO, Attorney-General, CPIB and Police able to investigate.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And if Mr Leon Perera – I suppose if he was part of any such organisation, would be the first one to make such a point.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But for the Government, with the systems in place and the variety of people who can lodge complaints and investigate – AGO, Attorney-General, you have CPIB, the Police – civil servants are obliged if they think that a Minister is doing wrong to take it up to a higher authority and, if they believe that the higher authority is not acting properly, they can take it up all the way.

sections.label: Independent ombudsman proposal criticised
sections.summary: Speaker says an ombudsman would require a huge taxpayer-funded structure and asks who guards the guards.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There seems to be a typical solution that is suggested for many different aspects of Government: set up an independent mechanism outside.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I mean, reading from his speech on 4 November 2020: "an ombudsman would function as an independent office to investigate complaints about administrative decisions or actions of a public agency, including delay, rudeness, negligence, arbitrariness, inconsistency, oppressive behaviour or unlawfulness".

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Every aspect of Government, anyone who is unhappy, go to an ombudsman, you have got to then set up an entire huge structure at the taxpayers' expense to investigate this, rather than having a proper legal process, including a complaint system, independent investigations set up, say, by the Police with some outside people sitting on it, or judicial review.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I mean, essentially, we can subcontract many aspects of Government, if we go down this route.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And it will not solve the problems, because who guards the guards?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, I would suggest we start with what is working well, what is not working, and for what is not working, how do we better do things.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If the suggestion is good and valid, we will study it.

sections.label: Police cameras solve cases
sections.summary: Police cameras island-wide helped solve over 6,000 cases, with unlicensed moneylending reports falling 94% from 2013 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In terms of detection and prevention of threats, Police Cameras deployed in public places island-wide have helped SPF solve more than 6,000 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Reports of crimes such as unlicensed moneylending have decreased by 94% from 2013 to 2021, between January and June, at approximately 2,100 HDB blocks installed with cameras.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: SPF will now expand its camera networks to more than 200,000 cameras by 2030 to continue to safeguard our public housing estates.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As at end 2021, SPF has completed the installation of about 90,000 cameras at HDB blocks, multi-storey car parks, town centres, neighbourhood centres and hawker centres.

sections.label: VEEN system implementation date
sections.summary: The VEEN system will be implemented in the first quarter of 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The VEEN system will be implemented in the first quarter of 2023.

sections.label: Automated Clearance Initiative expansion
sections.summary: ICA will introduce the Automated Clearance Initiative this year and double automated lanes at Changi Airport over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: ICA will introduce the Automated Clearance Initiative this year to allow more eligible visitors to use automated clearance facilities, without the need for prior application.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked if this will increase the immigration clearance time for Singaporeans since we will have a larger pool of travellers eligible for automated clearance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We can clear a traveller at the automated lane in less than half the time, compared to the manual counter.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, over the next three years, ICA will double the number of automated lanes at Changi Airport.

sections.label: SPS videoconferencing rehabilitation programmes
sections.summary: Since 2020, SPS has used videoconferencing for its rehabilitation programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since 2020, SPS has used videoconferencing for its rehabilitation programmes.

sections.label: HTX developing HEIDI cloud platform
sections.summary: HTX is developing HEIDI, a dedicated cloud platform.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: HTX is developing HEIDI, or Hyperscale Enterprise Intelligent Digital Infrastructure, a dedicated cloud platform.

sections.label: National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recidivism
sections.summary: In 2018, the NCPR was set up to oversee national efforts on offending, re-offending and rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In 2018, we set up the National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recidivism, or NCPR, to oversee national efforts to prevent offending and re-offending and enhance the rehabilitation of offenders.

sections.label: Youth offender and recidivism figures
sections.summary: Youth offenders decreased by 28% over the past decade, with recidivism rates of 26.4% and 14.9% for two cohorts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Thanks to the hard work of the agencies and our partners, we have seen the number of youth offenders decreased by 28% over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The two-year recidivism rate among youth offenders aged under 20 who were under the charge of the Singapore Prison Service was 26.4% for the 2019 release cohort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The three-year recidivism rate of youth offenders aged under 16 who were on MSF's Guidance Programme, Probation or Youth Homes was 14.9% for the 2016 release cohort.

sections.label: CNB rolling out CoSS
sections.summary: CNB will roll out CoSS progressively, with full islandwide implementation by March next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: If necessary, supervisees will be referred to the appropriate agencies for follow-up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that CNB will be rolling out CoSS progressively, with full implementation islandwide by March next year.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim network for ex-offenders
sections.summary: A network of 26 Malay/Muslim organisations and 11 M3@Towns was launched in November 2021 to support inmates, ex-offenders and their families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In November 2021, a network comprising 26 Malay/Muslim organisations (MMOs) and 11 M³@Towns was launched to strengthen collaboration and support for inmates, ex-offenders and their families.

sections.label: Dadah Itu Haram campaign participation
sections.summary: Over 230 volunteers and 340 partners took part in the Dadah Itu Haram campaign, reaching over 650,000 participants through more than 140 co-created events.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Currently, we have more than 230 volunteers and advocates, along with 340 partners comprising various Malay/Muslim organisations, community groups, special interest groups, barber shops and eateries, participating in the campaign.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Their efforts ensured that the "Dadah Itu Haram" campaign reached out to over 650,000 participants through more than 140 co-created events.

sections.label: NS operational requirements and HomeTeamNS clubhouse
sections.summary: SPF and SCDF will adjust operational requirements so more NSmen can take frontline roles, and the HomeTeamNS@Bedok Clubhouse opens at year end.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: SPF and SCDF will be adjusting operational requirements so that more NSmen, especially those with slight physical or medical limitations, can take on more frontline roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We are also looking at ways of improving the touchpoints for our NSmen for a more positive NS experience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This year, we commemorate 55 years of National Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: It is timely that we will be officially opening the HomeTeamNS@Bedok Clubhouse at the end of the year.

sections.label: Community Watch Scheme launch
sections.summary: In 2021, the Police launched the Community Watch Scheme to build a volunteer network to fight crime.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In 2021, the Police launched the Community Watch Scheme (CWS) to build a volunteer network to fight crime.

sections.label: New debt collection regulatory framework
sections.summary: A new debt collection regulatory framework will be put in place, involving a licensing regime and restrictions on debt collectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We have listened carefully to the feedback from the ground.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We intend to put in place a new debt collection regulatory framework to address this issue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: This framework will involve a licensing regime and introduce restrictions on what debt collectors can or cannot do.

sections.label: E-Commerce Marketplace Transaction Safety Ratings
sections.summary: MHA will introduce the E-Commerce Marketplace Transaction Safety Ratings later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: For example, later this year, MHA will be introducing the E-Commerce Marketplace Transaction Safety Ratings.

sections.label: CDSA money laundering amendments
sections.summary: MHA will amend the CDSA to allow money laundering offences at lower culpability levels, scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To address this issue, MHA will be making amendments to the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act or CDSA, to allow money laundering offences to be made out at lower levels of culpability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: These amendments are currently scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2022.

sections.label: Security officers training and wages
sections.summary: From 1 July 2023 security officers must complete RTT training before deployment, and PWM gives six-year wage increases to over 40,000 officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To continue raising the professionalism of our security industry partners, with effect from 1 July 2023, all security officers must complete the "Recognise Terrorist Threats" (RTT) training before they can be deployed at any site.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The PWM recommendations will provide a six-year schedule of sustained wage increases for more than 40,000 resident security officers.

sections.label: Ombudsman adoption by countries
sections.summary: The speaker asks why so many countries institute an independent ombudsman with investigative powers against the executive government if it is a bad idea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: My question would be that if instituting an independent organisation with investigative powers against the executive government, such as an ombudsman, is such a bad idea, why are so many countries doing that?

sections.label: Ombudsman reporting to Parliament
sections.summary: The speaker argues law enforcement sits within the executive, while an ombudsman would report to Parliament, placing it differently organisationally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So that is the first point I wanted to put across.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I think, fundamentally, the main argument for this ombudsman comes down to the fact that, currently, law enforcement institutions sit on the organisation chart within the executive Government, they are within that command and control hierarchy at the end of the day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: An ombudsman would report to Parliament in the manner that I outlined in that earlier speech and that means that it sits fundamentally in a different place organisationally.

sections.label: Agencies reporting to President
sections.summary: The speaker refers to an earlier response and states that the same agencies can report directly to the President.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Then that is the point I make in my earlier response to him.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And today, the very same agencies can report directly to the President and I have explained how that is so.

sections.label: Survey on mandatory death penalty
sections.summary: A survey of Singapore residents included a 2021 part on mandatory death penalty, with figures given, but results are still being analysed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The first question relates to a survey amongst Singapore residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And then 2021, on my instructions, a part of the survey specifically focused on mandatory death penalty.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And the figures I gave were for mandatory death penalty.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But having said that, I have to put a caveat, as I said, there is a statistical methodology and this survey has been completed fairly recently, the results are still being analysed.

sections.label: Survey on regional drug traffickers
sections.summary: The speaker says a survey on the region many drug traffickers come from will be made public without harming Singapore's interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, the survey that Mr Singh spoke about or referred to my speech, where I spoke about a survey in the region where not a small number, well, many of our drug traffickers come from.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think it is important and I have given instructions for it to be made public in some form, in a way that will not prejudice Singapore's public interest and foreign policy interest.
